estimate.damage_summary: During a drive, the laptop was thrown against the car door when the driver swerved, cracking its screen and damaging the lower-right corner/housing. The pre-existing lid scuff was not caused by the event.
estimate.policy_notes: The description indicates portable-equipment accidental-damage cover; this assessment assumes the schedule agrees that peril and co-insures household contents. Necessary repair of event-damaged parts is covered, with no depreciation for the same-model equivalent; the policy does not cover polishing a pre-existing scuff. Necessary diagnostic costs are covered under 5.2.3, subject to its EUR 250 gross per-event cap. No proportional reduction is stated.

lines.rationale: The cracked screen is confirmed as event damage, and replacing the complete display assembly is a plausible repair where the glass is not separately replaceable. The estimate allows for a standard-equivalent assembly and repair labour, not an upgrade.

The lower-right corner damage is described as part of the same impact, and replacing the damaged housing shell is a plausible repair. One repair is justified; the price range allows for a standard shell and labour.

lines.invoice_text: Polish of pre-existing lid scuff (surface only, does not affect operation)
lines.rationale: The scuff pre-dated the event and is a cosmetic surface condition, not damage caused by the impact. Its polishing is excluded as work beyond making good the event damage under 7.1.5 and 7.1.11; the stated price range is only an as-if-valid estimate.

A diagnostic inspection to establish the damage and repair scope is expressly reimbursable under 5.2.3, and the insured impact is described. One inspection is plausible; reimbursement remains subject to the EUR 250 gross per-event cap and any applicable deductible.
